sentences.en: I'm Gemma Spake, and welcome back to The Psychology of Your Twenties, the podcast where we talk through the biggest changes, moments, and transitions of our 20s
sentences.zh: 我是 Gemma Spake，欢迎回到《The Psychology of Your Twenties》，这是一档探讨我们 20 多岁时所经历的最大变化、时刻和转折点的播客，

sentences.en: and what they mean for our psychology.
sentences.zh: 以及它们对我们心理意味着什么。

sentences.en: Hello, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the show.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到节目。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到播客。

sentences.en: New listeners, old listeners, wherever you are in the world.
sentences.zh: 无论你是新听众还是老听众，无论你身在世界何处。

sentences.en: Before we get into it, two things for you today.
sentences.zh: 在开始之前，今天有两件事要告诉大家。

sentences.en: Number one, this episode and many others are now on Netflix.
sentences.zh: 第一，这一集和许多其他集现在已经在 Netflix 上线了。

sentences.en: So if you want a video version of this very episode, you can go and watch it over there.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你想看这一集的视频版本，可以去那边观看。

sentences.en: It really helps us out.
sentences.zh: 这对我们真的很有帮助。

sentences.en: And secondly, we have launched a really exciting new project on Substack that I don't think many of you know about.
sentences.zh: 第二，我们在 Substack 上启动了一个非常令人兴奋的新项目，我想你们很多人还不知道。

sentences.en: It's called the Study of the Week group.
sentences.zh: 它叫“每周研究小组”。

sentences.en: Basically, every week, I send you an academic study broken down into simple English and simple findings.
sentences.zh: 基本上，每周我都会向你发送一项学术研究，并将其拆解成简单的英语和简单的结论。

sentences.en: It goes straight to your inbox.
sentences.zh: 它会直接发送到你的收件箱。

sentences.en: We are doing 52 studies in 52 weeks to help make you smarter, to help give you interesting knowledge about human psychology,
sentences.zh: 我们将在 52 周内完成 52 项研究，旨在让你变得更聪明，为你提供关于人类心理学的有趣知识，

sentences.en: to use at work, in your relationships, with other people.
sentences.zh: 让你在工作、人际关系以及与他人相处时都能用到。

sentences.en: And it's really easy to sign up.
sentences.zh: 注册非常简单。

sentences.en: Just go to Substack, type in your email, and subscribe, and you get access every single week.
sentences.zh: 只需前往 Substack，输入你的电子邮件并订阅，你每周都能收到内容。

sentences.en: It is also a great way to support me and my work independently if you feel called to do so.
sentences.zh: 如果你愿意的话，这也是支持我和我独立工作的好方法。

sentences.en: Okay, enough self-promotion for one episode.
sentences.zh: 好了，这一集自我推销就到此为止。

sentences.en: I always hate doing that.
sentences.zh: 我一直很讨厌做这件事。

sentences.en: It's literally my least favorite part of making the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 这简直是我制作播客时最不喜欢的部分。

sentences.en: But this is my favorite part, which is talking about the psychology of common phenomena that apply to our 20s and beyond.
sentences.zh: 但我最喜欢的部分是探讨适用于我们 20 多岁及以后的常见现象背后的心理学。

sentences.en: And this episode, these are just my favorite kinds.
sentences.zh: 而这一集，正是我最喜欢的主题。

sentences.en: It's going to be so good because we are talking about the psychology of angel numbers.
sentences.zh: 这一集会非常精彩，因为我们要讨论的是“天使数字”背后的心理学。

sentences.en: Angel numbers are these numerical symbols that guide us, direct us, comfort us during times of transition and sometimes pain
sentences.zh: 天使数字是那些在过渡时期，有时是在痛苦、

sentences.en: and growth and uncertainty, but also just in everyday life.
sentences.zh: 成长和不确定时期，甚至是在日常生活中，指引我们、引导我们、安慰我们的数字符号。

sentences.en: It is the 4-4-4 you see on the microwave in the morning, and then the $2.22 your soda costs you at lunch, the $11.11 on your Uber's license plate.
sentences.zh: 比如你早上在微波炉上看到的 4-4-4，午餐时汽水价格里的 2.22 美元，还有优步车牌上的 11.11。

sentences.en: These numbers mean something to us.
sentences.zh: 这些数字对我们来说意义非凡。

sentences.en: And we know that because our brains can't help but notice them and feel drawn to them.
sentences.zh: 我们之所以知道这一点，是因为我们的大脑忍不住会注意到它们，并被它们所吸引。

sentences.en: Why is that?
sentences.zh: 这是为什么呢？

sentences.en: What is it about those numbers that presents us with so much psychological clarity and direction, and what does the science support about the mystical spiritual side of this?
sentences.zh: 这些数字究竟有什么魔力，能为我们提供如此多的心理清晰度和方向感？科学对于这种神秘的灵性层面又有何支持？

sentences.en: That is what we're going to discuss, as well as some insane plot twists to do with spiritual gurus and the women and the woman, I should say, who popularized angel numbers.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们要讨论的内容，此外还有一些关于灵性导师以及推广天使数字的女性（我应该说是那位女性）的疯狂剧情反转。

sentences.en: This episode takes many, many strange directions, but the psychology and the science is always fascinating.
sentences.zh: 这一集会走向许多非常奇怪的方向，但心理学和科学的部分总是引人入胜的。

sentences.en: So without further ado, let's get into it.
sentences.zh: 那么，废话不多说，让我们开始吧。

sentences.en: So first and foremost, before the psychology of angel numbers, what is the history of angel numbers?
sentences.zh: 首先，在探讨天使数字的心理学之前，天使数字的历史是什么？

sentences.en: Where do they originally come from?
sentences.zh: 它们最初来自哪里？

sentences.en: So angel numbers in the way we talk about them now are actually a very modern spiritual concept.
sentences.zh: 我们现在所谈论的天使数字，实际上是一个非常现代的灵性概念。

sentences.en: They are as modern as the invention and widespread use of numbers, which has actually only been quite a recent thing in human history,
sentences.zh: 它们和数字的发明及广泛使用一样现代，而这在人类历史上其实是很近的事情，

sentences.en: but they draw from two much, much older traditions, which is the belief that small things can act as messages from a higher power,
sentences.zh: 但它们借鉴了两个古老得多的传统：一是相信微小的事物可以作为来自更高力量的信息，

sentences.en: and also the belief that groupings of certain things carry hidden symbolic meaning, like seeing three crows or five coins or six donkeys, whatever it is.
sentences.zh: 二是相信某些事物的组合带有隐藏的象征意义，比如看到三只乌鸦、五枚硬币或六头驴，无论是什么。

sentences.en: An interesting part of this is the history of numbers themselves, because it has evolved in stages from basic counting and tallying,
sentences.zh: 其中一个有趣的部分是数字本身的历史，因为它经历了从基础计数和刻痕，

sentences.en: where people would carve strikes into walls or wood to keep track of things into the invention of the abacus.
sentences.zh: 即人们在墙壁或木头上刻下痕迹来记录事物，到算盘的发明等阶段。

sentences.en: And now the numerical system that we know of today, which was created by Indian and Arabic mathematicians,
sentences.zh: 而我们今天所知的数字系统，是由印度和阿拉伯数学家创造的，

sentences.en: this led to the, I wouldn't say creation, but the development of what we now have, which is numerology, the broader belief that numbers have divine,
sentences.zh: 这导致了——我不会说是创造，而是发展了我们现在所拥有的命理学，即一种更广泛的信仰，认为数字具有神圣的、

sentences.en: mystical, or symbolic significance, and they shape the structure of our reality.
sentences.zh: 神秘的或象征性的意义，并且它们塑造了我们现实的结构。

sentences.en: Now, numerology dates back centuries, and one of the earliest figures connected to this movement is Pythagoras.
sentences.zh: 命理学可以追溯到几个世纪前，与这一运动相关的最早人物之一是毕达哥拉斯。

sentences.en: He's a very ancient Greek philosopher.
sentences.zh: 他是一位非常古老的希腊哲学家。

sentences.en: You have definitely heard his name before.
sentences.zh: 你肯定听说过他的名字。

sentences.en: Probably in a high school math class, he's also the man who created Pythagorean theorem.
sentences.zh: 可能是在高中数学课上，他也是创造毕达哥拉斯定理的人。

sentences.en: His equation for triangles, I don't know if you remember it, like A plus B equals C, A squared, B squared, C squared.
sentences.zh: 他关于三角形的方程，我不确定你是否还记得，比如 A 加 B 等于 C，A 平方、B 平方、C 平方。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: I haven't done math in a while.
sentences.zh: 我已经很久没做数学题了。

sentences.en: But he was also the founder of a broader movement, a broader movement that basically believed that the universe is governed by mathematical harmony.
sentences.zh: 但他也是一个更广泛运动的创始人，这个运动基本上认为宇宙是由数学和谐所支配的。

sentences.en: Obviously, Pythagoras wasn't talking about angel numbers at the time.
sentences.zh: 显然，毕达哥拉斯当时并没有谈论天使数字。

sentences.en: I'm not going to reach that far.
sentences.zh: 我不会牵强附会。

sentences.en: That wasn't his theory.
sentences.zh: 那不是他的理论。

sentences.en: But he was talking about this broader tradition that
sentences.zh: 但他谈论的是这个更广泛的传统，即

sentences.en: numbers reflect the hidden order of things.
sentences.zh: 数字反映了事物的隐藏秩序。

sentences.en: They have this deeper, more interconnected, overarching meaning that we can access through their presence,
sentences.zh: 它们有一种更深层、更相互关联、更宏大的意义，我们可以通过它们的存在来获取，

sentences.en: and they reveal something like basically beneath the surface of ordinary life.
sentences.zh: 它们揭示了普通生活表面之下的一些东西。

sentences.en: Now, the other strand of this beyond Pythagoras and his idea of mathematical, I don't know, alignment, is the idea of angels,
sentences.zh: 现在，除了毕达哥拉斯和他关于数学——我不知道该怎么说——一致性的想法之外，另一个分支是天使的概念，

sentences.en: which show up a lot more in Western cultures with Christianity, maybe Judaism as well, Islam.
sentences.zh: 这在西方文化中出现得更多，伴随着基督教，也许还有犹太教和伊斯兰教。

sentences.en: This idea of spiritual beings that act as intermediaries or messengers from a higher power.
sentences.zh: 这种灵性存在的概念，充当了来自更高力量的中间人或信使。

sentences.en: In Christianity specifically, angels are often understood as these creatures that serve God.
sentences.zh: 特别是在基督教中，天使通常被理解为侍奉上帝的生物。

sentences.en: They offer protection.
sentences.zh: 它们提供保护。

sentences.en: They appear at important moments in biblical stories.
sentences.zh: 它们出现在圣经故事的重要时刻。

sentences.en: The word angel itself comes from the Greek word angelos, meaning messenger.
sentences.zh: “天使”（angel）这个词本身来自希腊语“angelos”，意为信使。

sentences.en: And this again ties into this belief that guidance can be communicated through signs.
sentences.zh: 这再次与那种认为可以通过迹象传达指引的信仰联系在一起。

sentences.en: Those two things combined create angel numbers.
sentences.zh: 这两者结合在一起就创造了天使数字。

sentences.en: So this concept of angelic protection and guidance, through numbers, through anything, that is a very ancient concept.
sentences.zh: 所以，这种通过数字、通过任何事物获得天使保护和指引的概念，是一个非常古老的概念。

sentences.en: It borrows from some very, very old principles and religions.
sentences.zh: 它借鉴了一些非常、非常古老的原则和宗教。

sentences.en: But angel numbers are just, I guess, not even the newest, but a more recent kind of development.
sentences.zh: 但天使数字只是，我想说，甚至不是最新的，而是一种更近期的发展。

sentences.en: The idea of repeating angel numbers, seeing angel numbers, is a very modern phenomena, primarily caused by the rise of New Age spirituality,
sentences.zh: 重复出现天使数字、看到天使数字的想法是一个非常现代的现象，主要是由新时代灵性的兴起引起的，

sentences.en: specifically the work of an American author called Doreen Virtue.
sentences.zh: 特别是美国作家 Doreen Virtue 的作品。

sentences.en: She popularized this idea that repeated number sequences could be interpreted as messengers from angels or spiritual guides.
sentences.zh: 她普及了这样一种观点：重复的数字序列可以被解释为来自天使或灵性向导的信使。

sentences.en: She wrote this huge series of books about it.
sentences.zh: 她为此写了一系列巨大的书。

sentences.en: It made her a multi-millionaire.
sentences.zh: 这让她成为了千万富翁。

sentences.en: She was on Oprah.
sentences.zh: 她还上过奥普拉脱口秀。

sentences.en: It just blew up.
sentences.zh: 它彻底火了。

sentences.en: It was like the big thing of the early 2000s.
sentences.zh: 这就像是 21 世纪初的一件大事。

sentences.en: Something really interesting, though, an interesting twist, is that Doreen actually underwent a whole religious conversion in like 2017.
sentences.zh: 不过，有一个非常有趣的反转是，Doreen 实际上在 2017 年左右经历了一次彻底的宗教皈依。

sentences.en: Like 10, maybe like 20 years after she,
sentences.zh: 就像在，也许是 20 年后，她，

sentences.en: I don't even know what the right word is, popularized the idea, she like completely renounced it.
sentences.zh: 我甚至不知道用什么词才准确，普及了这个想法，她就完全否定了它。

sentences.en: She became a complete born-again, fundamentalist Christian, and she's publicly stated that she no longer believes in angel numbers.
sentences.zh: 她成为了一名彻底的重生派原教旨主义基督徒，并公开声明她不再相信天使数字。

sentences.en: She doesn't think they're spiritually valid.
sentences.zh: 她认为它们在灵性上是无效的。

sentences.en: She has this whole YouTube show where she talks about it.
sentences.zh: 她有一个专门的 YouTube 节目来谈论这件事。

sentences.en: So if you want to go look that up, it's very interesting.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你想去查一下，那非常有趣。

sentences.en: She literally did an interview with, I don't know if you know the magazine, The Cut, which, by the way, one of my favorites, but she basically says, I regret this.
sentences.zh: 她甚至接受了——我不知道你是否知道那本杂志，《The Cut》，顺便说一下，这是我最喜欢的杂志之一——的采访，但她基本上说，我后悔了。

sentences.en: I regret popularizing angel numbers.

sentences.en: And 9-9-9-9 is usually interpreted as completion.
sentences.zh: 而 9-9-9-9 通常被解读为圆满。

sentences.en: It's the end, it's the last one kind of in that sequence.
sentences.zh: 这是终点，是该序列中的最后一个。

sentences.en: It's closure, it's release, it's endings.
sentences.zh: 它代表结束、释放和终结。

sentences.en: My favourite one though, and my personal angel number, if one can call it that, is 1-2-3-4-12-34.
sentences.zh: 不过我最喜欢的一个，也是我个人的天使数字（如果可以这样称呼的话），是 1-2-3-4-12-34。

sentences.en: I am not kidding when I say I see this in some form every single day without fail.
sentences.zh: 我没开玩笑，我确实每天都能以某种形式看到它，无一例外。

sentences.en: Like literally every single day.
sentences.zh: 真的是每天。

sentences.en: I will wake up in the middle of the night, it will be 12-34am.

sentences.en: I will read the word count for a script, it will be 1,234 words.

sentences.en: Grab an Uber, 12-34 in the licence plate.

sentences.en: I literally cannot express to you how many ways I have seen this.
sentences.zh: 我真的无法向你表达我见过多少次这种情况。

sentences.en: I don't know what it fully believes.
sentences.zh: 我不知道它到底代表什么。

sentences.en: I think it means that you're building a good life.
sentences.zh: 我认为它意味着你正在构建美好的生活。

sentences.en: I think it means that you should stick to your goal.
sentences.zh: 我认为它意味着你应该坚持你的目标。

sentences.en: I think it represents progress and growth.
sentences.zh: 我认为它代表进步和成长。

sentences.en: That is definitely my favourite.
sentences.zh: 那绝对是我最喜欢的一个。

sentences.en: The thing is though, with all those, the meanings can be interpreted as one and the same.
sentences.zh: 但问题是，对于所有这些数字，其含义可以被解读为同一个意思。

sentences.en: They also aren't necessarily universal.
sentences.zh: 它们也不一定是普遍适用的。

sentences.en: That is so important to know.
sentences.zh: 这一点非常重要。

sentences.en: The woman who wrote this book, obviously like had an idea, but it doesn't really matter.
sentences.zh: 写这本书的女士显然有一个想法，但这并不重要。

sentences.en: It matters what it means to you.
sentences.zh: 重要的是它对你意味着什么。

sentences.en: It matters in many ways what it psychologically represents and what it needs to mean to you in this moment.
sentences.zh: 在很多方面，重要的是它在心理上代表什么，以及它在这一刻对你意味着什么。

sentences.en: And I think that's why they're so meaningful.
sentences.zh: 我认为这就是它们如此有意义的原因。

sentences.en: Not because they have a universal meaning, but because they allow for a level of flexibility in their interpretation.
sentences.zh: 不是因为它们有普遍的含义，而是因为它们在解读上具有一定的灵活性。

sentences.en: Just like a poem can mean different things at different stages of your life, or a song lyric feels like it was written just for you, even though thousands of people listen to
sentences.zh: 就像一首诗在你人生的不同阶段可以有不同的含义，或者一首歌词感觉像是专门为你写的一样，尽管有成千上万的人在听，

sentences.en: it, even though, you know, like a religious passage can comfort different people from completely different life circumstances, angel numbers work in a similar way.
sentences.zh: 尽管你知道，一段宗教经文可以安慰来自完全不同生活环境的人，天使数字的工作方式也类似。

sentences.en: Their meaning is not fixed.
sentences.zh: 它们的含义不是固定的。

sentences.en: They act as an emotional container and they give shape and they take shape and they are symbolic and they are important, often based on things that we are already feeling.
sentences.zh: 它们充当情感容器，赋予事物形状，并随之成形，它们具有象征意义，并且往往基于我们已经感受到的事物而变得重要。

sentences.en: And they just become a way of externalizing something that we already know as a deep truth.
sentences.zh: 它们只是成为了一种将我们已知深层真理外化出来的方式。

sentences.en: So why do they feel so significant to us?
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么它们对我们感觉如此重要呢？

sentences.en: Why is 111 a good sign?
sentences.zh: 为什么 111 是个好兆头？

sentences.en: Why is 333 a positive thing?
sentences.zh: 为什么 333 是一件积极的事情？

sentences.en: What does the psychology say about our attraction to these numbers?
sentences.zh: 心理学对我们被这些数字吸引有什么看法？

sentences.en: We are going to dive into that after this short break.
sentences.zh: 休息之后，我们将深入探讨这个问题。

sentences.en: Angel numbers feel significant.
sentences.zh: 天使数字让人感觉意义重大。

sentences.en: Firstly, because they often appear or we are more likely to notice them at emotionally significant points in our life.
sentences.zh: 首先，因为它们经常出现，或者我们更有可能在我们人生中情感重要的时刻注意到它们。

sentences.en: And this is not a coincidence.
sentences.zh: 这并非巧合。

sentences.en: It's not an accident.
sentences.zh: 这不是意外。

sentences.en: It occurs because a core principle in psychology is that we interpret the world primarily through our emotional state.
sentences.zh: 之所以发生这种情况，是因为心理学的一个核心原则是，我们主要通过自己的情绪状态来解读世界。

sentences.en: Our reality shapes our emotions, but it also happens the other way around as well.
sentences.zh: 我们的现实塑造了我们的情绪，但反之亦然。

sentences.en: Meaning how we feel influences what we notice, what feels important, and the life that we have.
sentences.zh: 意思是我们的感受影响了我们注意到的事物、感觉重要的事物，以及我们所拥有的生活。

sentences.en: Perception is everything.
sentences.zh: 感知就是一切。

sentences.en: A useful way of understanding this is through what we call the meaning maintenance model.
sentences.zh: 理解这一点的一个有用方法是通过我们所说的“意义维护模型”。

sentences.en: So in a 2006 paper published in the Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, the authors kind of made the suggestion that people have an inherent need for meaning.
sentences.zh: 在 2006 年发表于《人格与社会心理学杂志》的一篇论文中，作者提出人们对意义有着内在的需求。

sentences.en: This is an old idea.
sentences.zh: 这是一个古老的观点。

sentences.en: They really were able to articulate it in this study.
sentences.zh: 他们确实在这项研究中将其阐述得非常清楚。

sentences.en: We need to perceive events through the frame of mental representations to organize our perception of the world.
sentences.zh: 我们需要通过心理表征的框架来感知事件，以组织我们对世界的认知。

sentences.en: We have this deep need, basically, to experience the world as this coherent, meaningful, logical, organized thing.
sentences.zh: 我们基本上有一种深层的需求，即体验一个连贯、有意义、合乎逻辑且有组织的世界。

sentences.en: That is important to us as humans.
sentences.zh: 这对我们人类来说很重要。

sentences.en: When that sense of meaning is threatened, for example, when life feels confusing, when you've
sentences.zh: 当这种意义感受到威胁时，例如，当生活感觉混乱时，当你

sentences.en: gone through a terrible breakup and you don't believe in love anymore, when you have no idea
sentences.zh: 经历了一场糟糕的分手，不再相信爱情时，当你不知道

sentences.en: what you are doing with your life, when a sickness occurs, when something unfair happens, people
sentences.zh: 自己的人生要做什么时，当疾病发生时，当不公平的事情发生时，人们

sentences.en: often try to restore meaning in another way, such as through the guidance and presence of angel numbers.
sentences.zh: 往往会尝试通过其他方式恢复意义，例如通过天使数字的指引和存在。

sentences.en: This helps explain why angel numbers become compelling during periods of transition.
sentences.zh: 这有助于解释为什么天使数字在过渡时期变得引人注目。

sentences.en: Like our 20s, like after a divorce, like when you've just lost a job, like when you are moving through grief.
sentences.zh: 比如我们的 20 多岁，比如离婚后，比如刚丢了工作，比如正在经历悲伤时。

sentences.en: These are all moments where life feels temporarily very unstructured and your brain does not like that.
sentences.zh: 这些都是生活暂时感觉非常无序的时刻，而你的大脑不喜欢那样。

sentences.en: We are looking for anything that can provide emotional scaffolding and emotional meaning to life.
sentences.zh: 我们正在寻找任何能为生活提供情感支撑和情感意义的东西。

sentences.en: This raises another question.
sentences.zh: 这就引出了另一个问题。

sentences.en: Why those numbers, though?
sentences.zh: 不过，为什么偏偏是这些数字呢？

sentences.en: Why are our minds so ready to see meaning in repeated numbers in the first place rather than just something else?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们的思维首先就这么容易在重复的数字中看到意义，而不是其他东西？

sentences.en: Like why are those things a sign?
sentences.zh: 比如为什么这些东西是信号？

sentences.en: That brings us to the psychology of pattern recognition.
sentences.zh: 这就引出了模式识别的心理学。

sentences.en: One of my favorite, I love this, I could talk about this all day, our brains are constantly
sentences.zh: 我最喜欢的一个，我爱这个，我可以整天谈论这个，我们的大脑不断地

sentences.en: scanning the environment for things that are the same, for repetition, for connection, for rhythm, for signs.
sentences.zh: 扫描环境，寻找相同的事物、重复、联系、节奏和信号。

sentences.en: Basically, our brains want to make sense of our surroundings to keep us safe.
sentences.zh: 基本上，我们的大脑想要理解周围的环境以确保我们的安全。

sentences.en: If they can predict what's going to happen next, that gives them a better chance.
sentences.zh: 如果它们能预测接下来会发生什么，那它们就有更好的机会。

sentences.en: It's one of the most important things that our brains do.
sentences.zh: 这是我们大脑所做的最重要的事情之一。

sentences.en: The sheer fact that our brains are wired to recognize patterns are what helps us to do things
sentences.zh: 我们的大脑天生就能识别模式，这一事实帮助我们做到了

sentences.en: like learn languages or recognize faces or understand social cues or predict when we might be in danger.
sentences.zh: 学习语言、识别人脸、理解社交暗示或预测我们何时可能处于危险之中。

sentences.en: It is a core, if not most critical, part of our brains and our lives as humans.
sentences.zh: 这是我们大脑和人类生活中核心的，甚至是最关键的部分。

sentences.en: It helps us learn that if we do certain behaviors, certain outcomes are going to happen.
sentences.zh: 它帮助我们学习到，如果我们做出某些行为，就会产生某些结果。

sentences.en: Dark clouds mean rain.
sentences.zh: 乌云密布意味着要下雨。

sentences.en: If somebody treats you like this, then it's probably going to end this way.
sentences.zh: 如果有人这样对待你，那么结果很可能会是这样。

sentences.en: And our inability to interpret those patterns is often what gets us into trouble, not just in terms of survival, but in terms of emotional patterns as well.
sentences.zh: 而我们无法解读这些模式往往会让我们陷入麻烦，不仅是在生存方面，在情感模式方面也是如此。

sentences.en: Pattern detection is life-saving, not listening to it can also be life-changing.
sentences.zh: 模式检测可以救命，不听从它也可能改变人生。

sentences.en: The tricky thing is that a brain that is built to detect meaningful patterns will sometimes find meaning in places where the pattern is a little bit random.
sentences.zh: 棘手的是，一个旨在检测有意义模式的大脑，有时会在模式有点随机的地方找到意义。

sentences.en: Psychologists sometimes refer to this as apophenia, which means perceiving meaningful connections between unrelated or random things.
sentences.zh: 心理学家有时称之为“空想性视错觉”（apophenia），意思是感知到无关或随机事物之间有意义的联系。

sentences.en: In simple terms, it's when the mind sees a pattern and gives it significance, even when the pattern doesn't have an external cause.
sentences.zh: 简单来说，就是当大脑看到一个模式并赋予其重要性，即使该模式没有外部原因时。

sentences.en: Now, that goes against some of our beliefs about angel numbers, but it is a really important explanation for why our brains like angel numbers.
sentences.zh: 这与我们关于天使数字的一些信念相悖，但它是解释为什么我们的大脑喜欢天使数字的一个非常重要的原因。

sentences.en: There was a 2008 study published in Science, the journal Science, by Jennifer Whitson.
sentences.zh: 2008 年《科学》杂志发表了一项由詹妮弗·惠特森（Jennifer Whitson）进行的研究。

sentences.en: She's a psychologist whose work has explored control and uncertainty and pattern perception.
sentences.zh: 她是一位心理学家，她的工作探索了控制感、不确定性和模式感知。

sentences.en: And it gives us a really useful way to understand this.
sentences.zh: 它为我们理解这一点提供了一个非常有用的方法。

sentences.en: Across a series of several experiments, Jennifer found that when people felt a lack of control,
sentences.zh: 通过一系列实验，詹妮弗发现当人们感到缺乏控制感时，

sentences.en: they were more likely to perceive illusory or, I don't want to say delusional, but just patterns in general.
sentences.zh: 他们更有可能感知到虚幻的，或者说，我不想说是妄想，但就是一般的模式。

sentences.en: They were more likely to see, for example, images in visual noise.
sentences.zh: 例如，他们更有可能在视觉噪声中看到图像。

sentences.en: They were more likely to identify connections that were just objectively not there.
sentences.zh: 他们更有可能识别出客观上并不存在的联系。

sentences.en: When we feel in control, the world already feels organized enough.
sentences.zh: 当我们感到有控制力时，世界已经感觉足够有条理了。

sentences.en: We don't really need to look for extra signs.
sentences.zh: 我们真的不需要寻找额外的信号。

sentences.en: When we feel out of control, the mind becomes more motivated to restore order.
sentences.zh: 当我们感到失去控制时，大脑会更有动力去恢复秩序。

sentences.en: It searches for meaning.
sentences.zh: 它会寻找意义。

sentences.en: Now, this is the critical thing, because does that mean the meaning isn't there?
sentences.zh: 现在，这是关键所在，因为这是否意味着意义不存在呢？

sentences.en: No, those numbers are still there.
sentences.zh: 不，那些数字依然存在。

sentences.en: The guidance they provide is still real.
sentences.zh: 它们提供的指引依然是真实的。

sentences.en: It's just that you start looking for them more.
sentences.zh: 只是你开始更多地去寻找它们了。

sentences.en: Now, why are the numbers there?
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么这些数字会存在呢？

sentences.en: That's another question, right?
sentences.zh: 那是另一个问题，对吧？

sentences.en: There is this deep intersection between spirituality and psychology when it comes to these things
sentences.zh: 当涉及到这些事情时，灵性与心理学之间存在着深刻的交集，

sentences.en: that you can't disentangle and you can't completely ignore the fact that numbers do control the
sentences.zh: 你无法将其解开，也无法完全忽视数字确实控制着

sentences.en: world and that math is this wonderful thing and that numerology is a very valid way of interpreting life.
sentences.zh: 世界，数学是一门美妙的学科，而命理学是一种非常有效的解读生活的方式。

sentences.en: This is where the idea of confirmation bias comes in.
sentences.zh: 这就是“确认偏误”概念的用武之地。

sentences.en: Confirmation bias is the tendency to notice, remember, and give more weight to information that supports what we already believe or suspect.
sentences.zh: 确认偏误是指倾向于注意、记住并给予支持我们已有信念或怀疑的信息更多权重。

sentences.en: Confirmation bias is something that we are all subject to.
sentences.zh: 确认偏误是我们所有人都会受到的影响。

sentences.en: Again, it's part of our brains hardwiring.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，这是我们大脑硬连线的一部分。

sentences.en: There's no escaping it.
sentences.zh: 无法逃避。

sentences.en: It is an essential feature of human thinking.
sentences.zh: 它是人类思维的一个基本特征。

sentences.zh: 然后，每当你做出某个决定后看到数字 222，这就会为你证实这一点。

sentences.en: That is enough to feel like you must have been correct.
sentences.zh: 这足以让你觉得你一定是正确的。

sentences.en: But the thing is, is that you may not remember all the times you made a decision and you didn't see the number 222.

sentences.en: Now, again, does this mean that angel numbers should be completely discounted just because the science has another explanation for them?

sentences.en: But it's just important to understand these illusions and these biases that also contribute to them being upheld.

sentences.en: Another one is the frequency illusion.

sentences.en: You may, this is the best way to describe this is like you learn a new term or you learn a new word and suddenly like everybody is talking about it.

sentences.en: Or you're thinking about buying a certain car and then suddenly every single car you see is that car.
sentences.zh: 或者你正在考虑买某款车，然后突然间你看到的每一辆车都是那款车。

sentences.en: It can feel like it's completely by chance, but it's just that your brain has started to filter for important information.
sentences.zh: 这感觉完全是偶然的，但只是因为你的大脑已经开始过滤重要信息了。

sentences.en: It's just starting to filter for things that you have decided is critical or remains critical for you.
sentences.zh: 它只是开始过滤那些你已经决定是关键的，或者对你仍然关键的事物。

sentences.en: The world has not necessarily changed, but your attention has.
sentences.zh: 世界不一定改变了，但你的注意力改变了。

sentences.en: Attention really sits at the core of this.

sentences.en: And angel numbers, again, work in the same way.
sentences.zh: 而天使数字，同样以这种方式运作。

sentences.en: Once a certain number becomes meaningful to you, the way 1234 is meaningful to me, your brain starts treating that number as important.
sentences.zh: 一旦某个数字对你变得有意义，就像 1234 对我有意义一样，你的大脑就开始把那个数字视为重要信息。

sentences.en: You filter literally millions of pieces of information every single day.
sentences.zh: 你每天实际上过滤了数以百万计的信息片段。

sentences.en: But once something has been encoded as significant, it's just going to pop out from the background, right?

sentences.en: It's like recognizing the face of somebody that you know and love in a crowd.

sentences.en: And so that is the circular process of how an angel number becomes important to us and then continues to be something that we see.

sentences.en: And that brings me to another idea that's connected to angel numbers, which is pro-noia.
sentences.zh: 这让我想到了另一个与天使数字相关的概念，即“顺向思维”（pro-noia）。

sentences.en: Pro-noia is described as the opposite of paranoia.
sentences.zh: “顺向思维”被描述为“偏执”（paranoia）的对立面。

sentences.en: Paranoia is the fear or belief that people, systems, or forces are kind of conspiring against you.
sentences.zh: 偏执是指一种恐惧或信念，认为人们、系统或力量在某种程度上密谋反对你。

sentences.en: So pro-noia, by contrast, is the sense that the world is conspiring in your favor.
sentences.zh: 相比之下，顺向思维则是一种认为世界在为你提供助力的感觉。

sentences.en: Now, this term was introduced into psychological literature by this guy called Fred Goldner.
sentences.zh: 这个术语是由弗雷德·戈德纳（Fred Goldner）引入心理学文献的。

sentences.en: He was a sociologist at Queens College in New York, and he talked about it in this article he published in 1982.
sentences.zh: 他是纽约皇后学院的一位社会学家，他在1982年发表的一篇文章中谈到了这一点。

sentences.en: He described pro-noia as a positive counterpart to paranoia, a belief that others think well
sentences.zh: 他将顺向思维描述为偏执的积极对应物，即相信他人对你有好感，

sentences.en: of you, a belief that events are favorable towards you rather than unfavorable, a belief that the social world is organized more benevolently around you than negatively around you.

sentences.en: This is psychologically remarkable.

sentences.en: It is psychologically powerful.
sentences.zh: 这在心理学上非常强大。

sentences.en: And it's basically a more scientific version of what you focus on expands.

sentences.en: If you focus on the good, that expands.

sentences.en: Pro-noia means that there is benevolence in the timings of things, that things might be aligning, even if you do not fully understand how they are right now.
sentences.zh: 顺向思维意味着事物的时机中存在善意，意味着事物可能正在对齐，即使你现在还不完全理解它们是如何对齐的。

sentences.en: It means that you are protected.
sentences.zh: 它意味着你受到了保护。

sentences.en: Angel numbers create this gentle form of pro-noia and this greater sense of responsiveness to life because we feel more confident that things are going to go our way.
sentences.zh: 天使数字创造了这种温和的顺向思维，以及对生活更强的响应感，因为我们更确信事情会朝着我们希望的方向发展。

sentences.en: And this is the part of angel numbers that can't be dismissed.
sentences.zh: 这就是天使数字不可忽视的部分。

sentences.en: Whether you think they're pseudoscience or not, they genuinely help people.

sentences.zh: 它不能保证你的关系一定会成功，但它确实保证了你的内在状态可能会更加平稳。

sentences.en: And I think people who believe in angel numbers often get a lot of yuck from other people.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为相信天使数字的人经常受到他人的很多嘲讽。

sentences.en: And I just don't think that's fair.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这不公平。

sentences.en: And let's talk about it.
sentences.zh: 让我们来谈谈这件事。

sentences.en: I think people often make fun of angel numbers and people who believe in angel numbers because
sentences.zh: 我认为人们经常嘲笑天使数字和相信天使数字的人，因为

sentences.en: there's this idea that they're irrational and they're sentimental and it's really associated
sentences.zh: 有一种观点认为他们是不理性的、感性的，而且这真的与

sentences.en: with this like Delulu, like online spiritual culture of like luck and fate and destiny and like how unscientific is that?
sentences.zh: 那种“Delulu”（妄想）、网络灵性文化中的运气、宿命和命运有关，这有多不科学啊？

sentences.en: I think sometimes this criticism comes from a genuine concern that maybe angel numbers are
sentences.zh: 我认为有时这种批评源于一种真诚的担忧，即天使数字可能正在

sentences.en: encouraging magical thinking or poor decision making or again, a confirmation bias that allows people to do things that maybe aren't wise.
sentences.zh: 鼓励魔幻思维或糟糕的决策，或者再次强调了确认偏误，让人们去做一些可能并不明智的事情。

sentences.en: Like if angel numbers can be a guide for positive things, they can also be a guide for things
sentences.zh: 就像如果天使数字可以成为积极事物的指南，它们也可能成为

sentences.en: that maybe aren't what's best for you, like getting back with people you probably shouldn't, quitting jobs without a plan, that sort of thing.
sentences.zh: 对你而言并非最佳事物的指南，比如与不该复合的人复合、毫无计划地辞职等等。

sentences.en: I think the concern can be fair, especially if somebody is making major life choices based on only the presence of numbers without a plan.
sentences.zh: 我认为这种担忧可能是合理的，特别是如果有人仅仅根据数字的出现而没有计划就做出重大人生选择的话。

sentences.en: But a lot of the time, that's not why people are worried about it.
sentences.zh: 但很多时候，人们担心的并不是这个。

sentences.en: A lot of the time, I think people just want to criticize it.
sentences.zh: 很多时候，我认为人们只是想批评它。

sentences.en: People just want to make you feel inferior.
sentences.zh: 人们只是想让你感到自卑。

sentences.en: I think the mockery around angel numbers, specifically from a certain group of people, comes from a bit of a superiority complex.
sentences.zh: 我认为围绕天使数字的嘲讽，特别是来自特定人群的嘲讽，源于一种优越感。

sentences.en: It becomes this way of like performing intelligence and performing detachment.
sentences.zh: 这变成了一种展示智慧和表现超脱的方式。

sentences.en: There's often this tone when people criticize angel numbers of like,
sentences.zh: 当人们批评天使数字时，往往带着一种语气，好像是说：

sentences.en: I'm more intelligent than you.
sentences.zh: “我比你聪明。”

sentences.en: I would never believe in that.
sentences.zh: “我绝不会相信那种东西。”

sentences.en: I understand the science.
sentences.zh: “我懂科学。”

sentences.en: You're dumb.
sentences.zh: “你很蠢。”

sentences.en: I'm not.
sentences.zh: “我不是。”

sentences.en: Well, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我不知道。

sentences.en: I understand the science.
sentences.zh: “我懂科学。”

sentences.en: You understand the science.
sentences.zh: “你懂科学。”

sentences.en: You just listen to 30 minutes of it.
sentences.zh: 你只是听了30分钟而已。

sentences.en: And I think that that science and that research makes angel numbers even more compelling
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，正是这些科学研究让“天使数字”变得更加令人信服，

sentences.en: in terms of the way that they psychologically guide people and the way that they emotionally provide courage that is needed for a human to act.
sentences.zh: 因为它们在心理上引导人们，并在情感上为人类行动提供了所需的勇气。

sentences.en: Actually, in terms of the way that they enable agency and self-belief, I don't think that's something to be scoffed at.
sentences.zh: 事实上，就它们赋予人们能动性和自信心而言，我认为这不值得嘲笑。

sentences.en: I actually think that is a remarkably powerful thing to have at your disposal.
sentences.zh: 我甚至认为，能拥有这种心理辅助是非常强大的。

sentences.en: There's also a very gendered element here.
sentences.zh: 这里还有一个非常明显的性别因素。

sentences.en: Many forms of spiritual meaning making like tarot, like angel numbers, like birth charts,
sentences.zh: 许多形式的灵性意义构建，比如塔罗牌、天使数字、出生星盘，

sentences.en: which are also typically associated with young women, often receive an additional unfair amount of criticism as being cringe or silly or embarrassing or stupid.
sentences.zh: 这些通常与年轻女性联系在一起的事物，往往会受到额外且不公平的批评，被贴上“尴尬”、“愚蠢”、“丢人”或“无脑”的标签。

sentences.en: It is almost a trend to mock them, to think of them as like silly women's things and emotional and not rational and ridiculous.
sentences.zh: 嘲笑它们几乎成了一种潮流，人们认为这些是女性的无聊玩意儿，是感性的、非理性的、荒谬的。

sentences.en: And, you know, the man's view of life is about hard work and rationality.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，男性视角下的生活往往被定义为努力工作和理性至上。

sentences.en: And you believing in this shows that you don't believe in that.
sentences.zh: 而你相信这些，就表明你不认同那种价值观。

sentences.en: That's kind of an idea.
sentences.zh: 这大概就是某种偏见。

sentences.en: Humans engage in symbolic and irrational rituals all the time.
sentences.zh: 人类无时无刻不在进行各种象征性的、非理性的仪式。

sentences.en: Athletes wear lucky clothing.
sentences.zh: 运动员会穿幸运服。

sentences.en: Students use lucky pens.
sentences.zh: 学生会用幸运笔。

sentences.en: Football fans believe they can jinx a game by not doing a certain routine beforehand or doing a certain routine beforehand.
sentences.zh: 足球迷相信，如果不在赛前做某种特定的仪式，或者做了某种仪式，就会给比赛带来厄运或好运。

sentences.en: People knock on wood.
sentences.zh: 人们会敲木头祈求好运。

sentences.en: People say everything happens for a reason.
sentences.zh: 人们会说“万事皆有因”。

sentences.en: All of these things involve emotion.
sentences.zh: 所有这些行为都涉及情感。

sentences.en: They involve symbolism, uncertainty, and perceived meaning.
sentences.zh: 它们涉及象征意义、不确定性和感知到的意义。

sentences.en: And those things are the exact same psychological root as angel numbers.
sentences.zh: 而这些东西与天使数字的心理根源完全相同。

sentences.en: It's just packaged differently.
sentences.zh: 只是包装方式不同罢了。

sentences.en: The branding is literally just different.
sentences.zh: 品牌营销手段完全不同而已。

sentences.en: It's like the difference between Diet Coke and Coke Zero.
sentences.zh: 就像健怡可乐和零度可乐的区别。

sentences.en: It's just the gender that they're marketed towards.
sentences.zh: 区别仅仅在于它们针对的营销性别不同。

sentences.en: So we're not really talking about a difference in rationality at all.
sentences.zh: 所以我们谈论的根本不是理性上的差异。

sentences.en: The difference is actually more so in which rituals are socially legitimized, socially supported, and which aren't.
sentences.zh: 真正的区别在于哪些仪式在社会上是合法的、受支持的，而哪些不是。

sentences.en: I also think this mockery can come from, and maybe this is a stretch, but I think it is a discomfort with hope.
sentences.zh: 我还认为这种嘲笑可能源于——也许有点牵强——但我认为这是对“希望”的一种不安。

sentences.en: Feeling hopeful can be really vulnerable.
sentences.zh: 怀抱希望可能会让人感到非常脆弱。

sentences.en: To believe that something might be working out for you is to risk disappointment.
sentences.zh: 相信某事可能会如你所愿，就意味着要冒着失望的风险。

sentences.en: And cynicism protects you against that disappointment.
sentences.zh: 而愤世嫉俗能保护你免受那种失望。

sentences.en: If you never believe in signs, you never have to feel foolish for hoping, you can give distance.
sentences.zh: 如果你从不相信征兆，你就永远不必因为怀抱希望而感到愚蠢，你可以保持距离。

sentences.en: You can remain detached from longing and from wanting.
sentences.zh: 你可以让自己远离渴望和需求。

sentences.en: And I think that's a really critical part that people don't talk about.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个人们很少谈论的关键点。

sentences.en: It's easy to not believe in angel numbers because believing in them would mean that like the possibility of something good is possible and you could have some hope around that.
sentences.zh: 不相信天使数字很容易，因为相信它们意味着好事发生的可能性是存在的，你可能会因此产生希望。

sentences.en: And then what if you're disappointed?
sentences.zh: 但如果最后失望了怎么办？

sentences.en: I think there's some fear in that as well.
sentences.zh: 我认为这其中也存在某种恐惧。

sentences.en: So is it actually all that bad to believe in angel numbers?
sentences.zh: 那么，相信天使数字真的有那么糟糕吗？

sentences.en: In most cases, no, it's not.
sentences.zh: 在大多数情况下，并没有，一点也不。

sentences.en: In fact, it's maybe even a good thing.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这甚至可能是一件好事。

sentences.en: I would make the argument that it is.
sentences.zh: 我会说，它确实是好事。

sentences.en: With anything, though, there are a few things to look out for, and I would be remiss if I didn't mention them.
sentences.zh: 不过，无论做什么，都有一些需要注意的地方，如果我不提出来，那就是我的失职。

sentences.en: So I'm going to here.
sentences.zh: 所以我现在要提一下。

sentences.en: I think the main things to be cautious of with anything in this kind of new age spiritual realm is exploitation.
sentences.zh: 我认为在这一类新时代灵性领域中，最需要警惕的是剥削。

sentences.en: Any belief system that offers people comfort during periods of uncertainty and transition and confusion can also become something that is sold back to them and used to manipulate
sentences.zh: 任何在人们处于不确定、过渡和困惑时期提供慰藉的信仰体系，都可能被转手卖给他们，并被用来操纵

sentences.en: them.
sentences.zh: 他们。

sentences.en: And that's just an annoying part of human existence.
sentences.zh: 这只是人类生存中令人讨厌的一部分。

sentences.en: This is especially the case, in my opinion, in online spiritual spaces where we're sold
sentences.zh: 在我看来，在网络灵性空间中尤其如此，我们被兜售

sentences.en: more and more and more reassurance and more and more comfort packaged as personalized readings
sentences.zh: 越来越多的安慰，越来越多的以个性化解读

sentences.en: or intuitive messages from the universe when it may just be a way for somebody to make money off of you and you have to kind of be aware of people's human urges to exploit.
sentences.zh: 或来自宇宙的直觉信息为包装的慰藉，而这可能只是某些人从你身上赚钱的方式，你必须意识到人类利用他人的冲动。

sentences.en: A lot of people earn money through spiritual work and it's fair work and it's important work.
sentences.zh: 很多人通过灵性工作赚钱，这是公平的工作，也是重要的工作。

sentences.en: The issue is when certain people pry on people's vulnerabilities, pry on their anxiety in order
sentences.zh: 问题在于，当某些人利用人们的脆弱和焦虑，

sentences.en: to sell them a product and their own belief in the product is not there and their own good intentions are not there.
sentences.zh: 去向他们兜售产品，而他们自己并不相信这些产品，也没有善意时。

sentences.en: Someone may start with a harmless interest in angel numbers and slowly get pulled into this loop of needing more reassurance, one more reading, one more spiritual download, one
sentences.zh: 某人可能最初只是对天使数字有无害的兴趣，然后慢慢陷入这种循环：需要更多的安慰、更多的解读、更多的灵性下载、

sentences.en: more video telling them what this number means for this specific situation.
sentences.zh: 更多的视频来告诉他们这个数字对特定情况意味着什么。

sentences.en: And often the language used is really persuasive and really general because it wants to speak to anybody who is in a place of emotional uncertainty.
sentences.zh: 而且所使用的语言往往非常有说服力且非常笼统，因为它想触及每一个处于情感不确定状态的人。

sentences.en: That's often all of us, you know.
sentences.zh: 那通常就是我们所有人，你知道的。

sentences.en: It wants to relate to everybody so that they can make more money and so that they can kind of manipulate a system.
sentences.zh: 它想与每个人产生共鸣，这样他们就能赚更多的钱，从而操纵这个系统。

sentences.en: And it is important to be aware of that and to be aware of the psychological power of angel numbers and what they can do and the comfort they can offer people.
sentences.zh: 意识到这一点很重要，意识到天使数字的心理力量、它们的作用以及它们能为人们提供的安慰也很重要。

sentences.en: And just because we know that, it also means that people who have bad intentions know that as well.
sentences.zh: 仅仅因为我们知道这一点，也意味着那些心怀不轨的人同样知道这一点。

sentences.en: And we have to be aware as well of a dependency on external confirmation that some of these processes can create.
sentences.zh: 我们还必须意识到，其中一些过程可能会产生对外部确认的依赖。

sentences.en: Instead of learning to sit with ambiguity, to tolerate uncertainty, to just like trust your judgment, sometimes we can get desperate in our search for angel numbers or a sign.
sentences.zh: 与其学会与模糊共处、忍受不确定性、仅仅是相信自己的判断，有时我们在寻找天使数字或征兆时会变得绝望。

sentences.en: And when it doesn't come, it can be awful.
sentences.zh: 而当征兆没有出现时，那种感觉会很糟糕。

sentences.en: It can be awful.
sentences.zh: 真的会很糟糕。

sentences.en: And I want to say again, a lot of people engage with spiritual practices in a very sincere, honest, helpful way and an ethical way and with an intention of really guiding people.
sentences.zh: 我想再次强调，很多人以非常真诚、诚实、有益且合乎道德的方式参与灵性实践，并怀着真正引导他人的初衷。

sentences.en: But it's just worth being cautious and it's just worth knowing your source a little bit more.
sentences.zh: 但保持谨慎、多了解一下你的信息来源是值得的。

sentences.en: And also being okay with a little bit of uncertainty.
sentences.zh: 同时，也要学会接受一点点不确定性。

sentences.en: Like it's okay.
sentences.zh: 这没关系。

sentences.en: It's okay to not know.
sentences.zh: 不知道也没关系。

sentences.en: You know, also look at the example of Doreen Virtue, who we spoke about earlier.
sentences.zh: 你知道，看看我们之前提到的多琳·弗丘（Doreen Virtue）的例子。

sentences.en: Here is a woman who made millions and millions and millions of people and then basically reneged and said, oh, I actually, I don't believe in that.
sentences.zh: 这是一个曾经让数百万人追随，后来却基本上背弃了这一切，说“哦，其实我不相信那个”的女人。

sentences.en: And this article I was speaking about talks about these individuals who were just left like heartbroken and they'd made major life decisions on this woman's teachings.
sentences.zh: 我提到的那篇文章谈到了那些人，他们感到心碎，因为他们曾根据这个女人的教导做出了重大的人生决定。

sentences.en: They felt very scammed.
sentences.zh: 他们感到被欺骗了。

sentences.en: They felt very misled.
sentences.zh: 他们感到被误导了。

sentences.en: They felt even more confused because she's just a human.
sentences.zh: 他们感到更加困惑，因为她也只是个人。

sentences.en: Humans are fallible.
sentences.zh: 人是会犯错的。

sentences.en: Like it's difficult to put our hopes and fears at their feet.
sentences.zh: 把我们的希望和恐惧寄托在他们身上是很困难的。

sentences.en: One more thing that I think we should be aware of is the fixation and anxiety that can come with our belief in angel numbers.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们还应该意识到的一点是，对天使数字的信仰可能会带来执念和焦虑。

sentences.en: Not for everybody, but as much as there are positive, encouraging messages that come from angel numbers and seeing 222 or 1234 or 444 everywhere, the opposite can also be true.
sentences.zh: 不是对每个人都这样，但尽管天使数字和随处可见的222、1234或444能带来积极、鼓励的信息，反之亦然。

sentences.en: If we start to fixate on good numbers, we can also start to fixate on bad numbers, maybe interpreting certain numbers as omens or warnings or signs that something is going wrong.
sentences.zh: 如果我们开始执着于“好数字”，我们也会开始执着于“坏数字”，可能会把某些数字解读为预兆、警告或事情出错的信号。

sentences.en: We can also, if we don't see our angel number every day or regularly, we can start to feel exceedingly unsure of a decision.
sentences.zh: 如果我们不能每天或定期看到我们的天使数字，我们也会开始对某个决定感到极其不确定。

sentences.en: Like I'm not getting confirmation of this.
sentences.zh: 就像“我没有得到这个确认”。

sentences.en: Is this the right decision?
sentences.zh: 这是正确的决定吗？

sentences.en: Maybe it is, even if there's not a number to support that.
sentences.zh: 也许是，即使没有数字来支持它。

sentences.en: We can get into this trap of black and white thinking where we're trying to predict the future based on these neutral numbers that we notice.
sentences.zh: 我们可能会陷入非黑即白的思维陷阱，试图根据我们注意到的这些中性数字来预测未来。

sentences.en: At that point, the practice can shift from being a source of courage and meaning making and motivation and magic to being a big component of disorders like anxiety and OCD.
sentences.zh: 到了那个地步，这种实践就从勇气、意义构建、动力和魔法的源泉，变成了焦虑和强迫症等疾病的重要组成部分。

sentences.en: If you're waiting around to see if there is a numerical sign to make a decision about your
sentences.zh: 如果你一直在等待，看是否有数字征兆来决定你的

sentences.en: life, or if you are being put off doing something you know you need to do because of a so-called
sentences.zh: 生活，或者因为所谓的“坏数字”或因为没看到“好数字”而推迟做你明知该做的事，

sentences.en: bad number or because you haven't seen a good number, then I think that is the point where not everybody gets here, but it is the point where you might need to take a step back and
sentences.zh: 那么我认为这就是临界点——虽然不是每个人都会走到这一步，但这是你可能需要退后一步，

sentences.en: just be like, is this belief making my life bigger or smaller?
sentences.zh: 问问自己：这种信仰是让我的生活变得更广阔还是更狭隘了？

sentences.en: Belief, it's in the word, needs to make your life bigger.
sentences.zh: “信仰”这个词本身就意味着它应该让你的生活变得更广阔。

sentences.en: I think I would take it back to that core message.
sentences.zh: 我想我会回归到那个核心信息。

sentences.en: At the end of the day, you are the magic and you are the decision maker.
sentences.zh: 归根结底，你才是魔法本身，你才是决策者。

sentences.en: You are the one who has the say.
sentences.zh: 你才是那个有话语权的人。

sentences.en: You are conscious.
sentences.zh: 你有意识。

sentences.en: You make things happen.
sentences.zh: 你让事情发生。

sentences.en: You do the healing.
sentences.zh: 你完成了疗愈。

sentences.en: You push your own evolution forward.
sentences.zh: 你推动了自己的进化。

sentences.en: If you need a sign, if you need encouragement, that is not a bad thing.
sentences.zh: 如果你需要一个征兆，如果你需要鼓励，那并不是坏事。

sentences.en: Every human needs motivation in some form.
sentences.zh: 每个人都需要某种形式的动力。

sentences.en: Angel numbers don't do the work for you though, and they aren't the final be all, say all, end all of this situation.
sentences.zh: 但天使数字不会替你完成工作，它们也不是决定这件事的最终定论。

sentences.en: Again, I want to say I love the concept of angel numbers.
sentences.zh: 再次声明，我热爱天使数字这个概念。

sentences.en: They have provided so much comfort for me during really difficult times.
sentences.zh: 在非常困难的时期，它们给了我极大的安慰。

sentences.en: I went through a really terrible breakup.
sentences.zh: 我经历过一次非常糟糕的分手。

sentences.en: Angel numbers played a great role.
sentences.zh: 天使数字在其中发挥了很大的作用。

sentences.en: When I moved cities and I felt really, really lonely, they were a guiding light for me.
sentences.zh: 当我搬到新城市感到非常非常孤独时，它们是我的一盏指路明灯。

sentences.en: When I wanted to quit my job, I'm not going to lie and say I didn't see a 2-2-2 and think that was a good choice.
sentences.zh: 当我想辞职时，我不会撒谎说我没看到222并认为这是一个好选择。

sentences.en: They made the ordinary feel less hard and they made my life feel more meaningful and significant.
sentences.zh: 它们让平凡的生活感觉没那么艰难，让我的生活感觉更有意义和重要。

sentences.en: And I think the science behind why they made me feel that way makes them even more important
sentences.zh: 我认为它们之所以让我有这种感觉的科学依据，使它们对我来说

sentences.en: to me because it confirms that what I'm searching for, if I'm searching for something, I obviously already secretly, unconsciously want it.
sentences.zh: 更加重要，因为它证实了我在寻找的东西——如果我在寻找什么，我显然已经在潜意识里秘密地渴望它了。
